da-non-sequitur.evidence: Full review 2026-11-21. Rewritten. Improved: Habiro membership of Phi_q*tr_{M,l}(T_w) is now an explicit hypothesis of the statement (residue-at-root.md:2) with the open part sent to conj:gs-residue-at-root-existence; pi_n is constructed (threads x_N in Z[q]/(q;q)_N, Phi_n | 1-q^n | (q;q)_n), shown a ring hom and surjective, and the false identification of the projection with an analytic residue at a regular point is gone (the Habiro comparison is cited as not needed). The proof establishes the statement once the residue is read as pi_{n_l}. Remains: n_l is never defined in the statement or proof, and the step 'identifying Z[q]/Phi_{n_l}(q) with Z[zeta_l]' (prf:14) holds only if zeta_l is a primitive n_l-th root of unity, which nothing states; the statement also says 'Habiro completion of Z[q^{+-1}]' while the proof builds it from Z[q]. No empirical premise; no ruling conflict.

Re-stamp after PR #8818: the only .md change re-keys the root-of-unity evaluation remark from habiro2002 to habiro2004 §1.2, in a sentence the proof says it does not use. The argument is unchanged, so the 2026-11-21 verdict stands.

trap-nonspeakable.notes: NON-TRAP FINDING, not fixed (attribution/convention, needs the author): 'Equivalence with the analytic definition ... is the content of the Habiro-completion theorem \cite{habiro2002}: the cyclotomic projections agree with the analytic residue at zeta_l for any element of Zhat[q] that converges as a complex function on |q| > 1.' The convergence region looks inverted — Habiro-ring elements are sums a_n(q)(q;q)_n and (q;q)_n converges for |q| < 1 while growing for |q| > 1 — and I could not match the quoted equivalence to habiro2002, whose content is the cyclotomic completion and the unified WRT invariant rather than an analytic-residue comparison. Also inherits the zeta_l vs zeta_{n_l} index inconsistency recorded on residue-at-root.md, and identifies Z[q]/Phi_{n_l}(q) with Z[zeta_l] (a ring) where the proposition calls it the field Q(zeta_l).
